newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares fall for sixth day in a row.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares fall for sixth day in a row.

text.p: Slovenian shares continued on their downward trek on Monday, slipping 0.74 percent on low turnover as investors continued to take a wait-and-see stance.

"We are living in a time of uncertainty. There are no foreign investors except for a few speculators -- everyone is waiting for March 10, when banks are expected to set up custody accounts," said Peter Pirc, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska Banka.
Two weeks ago the central bank said that foreign investors would have to open special custody accounts in order to trade in Slovenian securities.
"Nobody knows what the banks will demand for opening these accounts -- and whether international investors find the costs are too high," said Milos Obed, a trader at A Banka.
"I am not afraid for the long term future of our market. Foreigners will definitely come back to the market," he added.

The 11-share SBI index fell 10.23 points or 0.74 percent to 1,374.80. The blue-chip index fell for the sixth consecutive day. Since February 17, the last day when the index rose, it has fallen 6.3 percent.
Overall 10 shares fell, three rose and one was unchanged, while 12 were untraded. Turnover fell to 107.2 million tolars from 131.5 million.
Drug maker Lek's A issue was the most active share, firming 0.43 percent to 28,200 tolars on volume of 1,971 shares for total turnover of 55.5 million tolars.
Brokerage Finmedia led the day's decliners, tumbling 11.79 percent to 12,350 tolars on volume of 50 shares.
Food producer Kolinska was the biggest gainer, firming 3.14 percent to 2,300 tolars on volume of 13 shares.
